title: silent canary throttles due to config-shadow and timestamp interpretation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers experienced unexplained 429/503 errors during a canary rollout that updated burst/quota metadata. Root cause appears to be a mismatch between the control-plane's canonical policy epoch and agent-side interpretation of burst windows combined with a config-shadowing bug in the proxy which caused silent requests to be dropped without clear metrics.
incident_timeline: 2025-03-02T09:12Z - PagerDuty alert: elevated 429s in hosted region us-west-2 for customers A and B
2025-03-02T09:20Z - Ops routed traffic away from the canary pool; errors decreased but persisted for dedicated/private tenants
2025-03-02T10:05Z - Investigation: discrepancy observed between control-plane policy version 3742 and agent lease epoch reported by private deploys (epoch 3740)
2025-03-02T11:30Z - Hotfix deployed: control-plane reverted the canary config and invalidated in-flight policy snapshots; 429s fell to baseline for hosted customers
2025-03-02T13:00Z - Dedicated and some private tenants continued seeing elevated 503s; network trace showed proxy returning 503 on admission checks when burst tokens should have been available
2025-03-02T15:10Z - Correlation found: feature flag 'apply-shadow-policies' introduced in canary caused proxy to read legacy quota keys for requests lacking the rollout header
2025-03-02T17:45Z - Temporary mitigation: proxy change to prefer explicit tenant-header and log shadow-policy-paths; roll-forward scheduled after validation
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy canary policy that introduces a 'shadow' migration key for backward compatibility
2) Send mixed traffic with and without the new rollout header from a multi-tenant client (mixing hosted and private agents)
3) Observe agent logs: some hosts apply epoch N policy while others continue operating on epoch N-2
4) Watch admission path: proxy consults legacy key when rollout header absent and returns 503 when cumulative burst accounting doesn't match agent's lease state
root_cause: A three-way interaction: 1) control-plane fast-rollout updated policy epochs without ensuring atomic snapshot propagation to private agents, 2) proxy feature 'config-shadowing' favored legacy quota keys for requests missing the new rollout header, and 3) agent-side timestamp interpretation of burst-window boundaries used wall-clock rounding that diverged across hosts. Together these caused admission checks to see negative available-burst values and silently drop or fail requests instead of returning an informative metric-tagged rejection.
mitigations: Immediate: revert canary, invalidate stale policy snapshots in control plane, and add emergency logging for shadow-policy paths
Short-term: patch proxy to treat absent rollout headers as explicit 'unknown' and always consult current policy epoch as authoritative
Customer-facing: notify impacted customers with incident timeline and targeted mitigations; open support tickets and offer dedicated capacity credits for SLAs affected
long_term_actions: 1) Implement epoch-consistency handshake: control plane must wait for confirmation of snapshot receipt from private agents before activating a new epoch for canaries
2) Replace shadow-key fallback with an explicit migration path and compatibility flag that requires agent opt-in rather than silent fallback
3) Normalize burst-window math across agent runtimes by switching to monotonic clocks and a shared rounding policy library
4) Add a QA scenario in the canary pipeline that simulates mixed-hosted/private traffic and validates admission paths under version skew
5) Extend observability: surface 'policy-age' and 'burst-soft-deny' metrics in Console with per-tenant tags and policy-epoch labels
postmortem_notes: Root cause is systemic and crosses runtime, proxy, and control-plane; single-team fixes are insufficient
Team retro scheduled 2025-03-12 to review rollout gating and QA improvements
We will require a checklist and automated smoke tests for any future policy epoch changes that affect burst/quota semantics
communication_log: 2025-03-02T12:00Z - Customer A Slack: "Customer A reported intermittent 429s starting at 09:05, engineering acknowledged and provided status updates every 30 minutes"
2025-03-02T12:45Z - Support update: issued temporary capacity credits to customers A and C and opened follow-up support cases
2025-03-03T09:00Z - External postmortem draft sent to impacted customers for review
notes: We discovered race window when invalidating snapshots; control plane invalidation previously relied on eventual GC which could leave agents reading stale policy for up to 2 minutes
Proxy logs had poor metric tagging for shadow-path decisions—added additional tags in PR 2411
Consider adding canary traffic mirroring to a 'dry-run' admission path to detect divergence before active rollout
